'''Selenne Bañuelos''' (born January 29, 1985){{r|cabirth}} is an American mathematician and associate professor of [[mathematics]] at [[California State University Channel Islands]]. Her research is in the areas of [[differential equation|differential]] and [[difference equations]] and [[dynamical systems]], with a focus on their applications to [[mathematical biology]].

==Early life, education, and career==
Bañuelos was born Selenne Hayde Torres-Garcia to Georgina Torres, Mexican immigrants who raised her in the community of Boyle Heights, east of downtown [[Los Angeles]].{{r|thesis}}{{r|lathisms}}  earned her [[Bachelor of Science|B.S.]] degree in mathematics from the [[University of California, Santa Barbara]] in 2007.<ref name=lathisms /> She was awarded a [[Ph.D.]] in applied mathematics from the [[University of Southern California]] (USC) in 2013.  Her dissertation ''Structured two-stage population model with migration between multiple locations in a periodic environment'' was supervised by Robert John Sacker.{{r|mg}}<ref name=thesis /> During her doctoral studies at USC, she was presented with the Department of Mathematics Denis Ray Estes Graduate Teaching Prize.  She was a co-founder of the USC chapter of [[SACNAS]].<ref name=lathisms />  Bañuelos was part of the SACNAS Chapter Leadership Institute Alumni for her work at USC.{{r|sacnas2}}

Bañuelos joined the faculty at [[California State University Channel Islands]] in 2014 as an assistant professor of mathematics.  She is currently an associate professor of mathematics.  She is co-advisor to the SACNAS chapter at Channel Islands, a mentor for Math Alliance{{r|alliance}}, and a mentor and advisor for the CSU Alliance PUMP (Preparing Undergraduates through Mentoring towards PhDs) Program.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-07-25 |title=Selenne Bañuelos - Faculty Biographies- CSU Channel Islands |url=https://ciapps.csuci.edu/FacultyBiographies/selenne.banuelos |access-date=2022-07-22 |website= |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210725102931/https://ciapps.csuci.edu/FacultyBiographies/selenne.banuelos |archive-date=25 July 2021 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

In 2014, Bañuelos was a Linton Poodry SACNAS Leadership Institute fellow {{r|sacnas1}} and in 2015, she was a [[Project NExT]], New Experiences in Teaching, fellow.<ref name=lathisms />

In 2018, Bañuelos was featured on the Lathisms calendar.<ref name=lathisms /> In 2020, she received the [[Mathematical Association of America]] [[Henry L. Alder Award]] for Distinguished Teaching.{{r|maa_alder}}{{r|csuci2}} She is included in deck 2 of EvenQuads which is a series of playing card decks that feature notable women mathematicians published by the [[Association for Women in Mathematics|Association of Women in Mathematics]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=PlayingCards_Deck2 |url=https://awm-math.org/publications/playing-cards/playingcards_deck2/ |access-date=2023-09-30 |website=Association for Women in Mathematics (AWM) |language=en-US}}</ref>
